video.title: The Most Profitable Side Hustle No One Is Doing Yet

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Derek, who turned a $250-300 Amazon inflatable movie screen bought as a Christmas gift into Backyard Movie Theater in North Dallas. After a windy first HOA booking flopped, he bought a 20 ft commercial screen from Alibaba (~$3,500 plus ~$1,000 shipping), plus a $1,100 projector and two $1,500 JBL speakers, and sells packages from $375 to $1,500. He also designed a custom indoor air-conditioned inflatable theater (about $3,500 all-in, $1,700 per booking) because Texas summer movies can't start before 9:30pm, and added a $20k LED dance floor rented at $3,000. He claims $10k of bookings in one week, about $40k last year and $90-100k expected this year at 70-80% margins, mostly from Facebook Marketplace and referrals.

speakers.name: Derek
speakers.description: Founder of Backyard Movie Theater (North Dallas); former commercial drone pilot; co-owns a drinkware business

ideas.name: Backyard outdoor movie theater rental
ideas.one_liner: Rent inflatable outdoor movie screen setups with projector, wired speakers and themed chairs for kids' parties, HOAs and schools.
ideas.customer: Families hosting birthday parties and movie nights, HOAs, schools
ideas.problem: People want a memorable movie-night event at home without owning equipment
ideas.offer: 20 ft commercial screen, projector, wired JBL speakers, packages with 6/10/20 inflatable, cinema or LED chairs; pre-show coming attractions and music

pricing.notes: Nine times out of ten customers choose a package; about four top-tier bookings so far.

acquisition_channels.details: Listed on Facebook Marketplace to test demand; still the main source.

quote.text: You're relying on Facebook Marketplace. Yeah. Okay. Referrals
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Neighbours and parents at events asked for bookings; schools followed.
He emails prospects (unspecified) to see what comes through.

ideas.delivery: Derek personally delivers, sets up, runs wiring and operates the show.
ideas.startup_cost: $250-300 initial Amazon screen; ~$10k for commercial hardware
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Immediately after listing on Marketplace (first booking an HOA)

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings and inbound enquiries can be handled by agents; Facebook Marketplace posting itself is manual-ish.

onboarding.how: Online booking with package selection and deposits.

delivery.how: Physical delivery, setup and operation on site; could hire crews but always human.

billing.how: Online payments, often paid in advance.

support.how: Agents can answer questions and reschedule.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK but weather (wind, rain) is a bigger issue; UK summer darkness comes even later (~10pm), which strengthens the indoor version. Public screenings may need film licences (e.g. Filmbank/MPLC); event insurance needed.

ideas.name: Indoor air-conditioned inflatable movie theater
ideas.one_liner: A custom-designed, carpeted, LED-lit inflatable room with four AC units so kids' movie nights can start in daylight.
ideas.customer: Affluent families, often on multi-acre properties
ideas.problem: In Texas summer it isn't dark until 9:30pm, too late for kids' movies, and you can't project in daylight
ideas.offer: Inflatable dark room with screen inside, carpet, LED lighting, 4 air conditioners, same projector and speakers

pricing.notes: About 10 bookings; no upselling, customers who haggle aren't the target.

ideas.delivery: Custom inflatable from an overseas manufacturer, ~2 months to design and 3-4 months shipping; set up by Derek.
unit_economics_claims: Inflatable $2,000, carpet ~$400, used ACs ~$150-200 each; ~$3,500 all in

acquisition.how: Inbound listings and enquiry handling can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: UK late summer sunsets and rain make an indoor inflatable cinema arguably more useful; AC less needed than in Texas.

risks: Electrical load of multiple AC units

ideas.name: LED dance floor rental
ideas.one_liner: Rent modular 2 ft LED dance floor panels for weddings, milestone parties and school end-of-year events.
ideas.problem: Events want a wow-factor dance floor
ideas.offer: 8x8 up to 24x24 LED floors (24x24 fits ~100-130 people); extra power kit to run three bookings a day

pricing.notes: Spent a year negotiating with the manufacturer.

acquisition_channels.details: Cross-sold from movie nights where kids danced after the film.

ideas.delivery: Panels delivered and assembled on site.
unit_economics_claims: 24x24 floor cost ~$20,000; rents at $3,000 (~7-8 rentals to pay off)

uk_applicability.notes: LED dance floor hire is an established UK wedding service; competition exists.

risks: $20k upfront with only one rental so far

tactics.name: Test demand by listing a consumer item on Marketplace
steps: Buy a cheap consumer version (~$300 inflatable screen)
List it on Facebook Marketplace to see if anyone books
Take the first booking even if unprepared
Reinvest in commercial-grade gear once demand is proven

quote.text: If you are prepared, you've waited too long
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Package-based pricing
steps: Offer a base package (screen + speakers, $375)
Add tiers by chair count and type (6, 10, 20; cinema or LED)
Top tier at $1,500
Most customers pick a package rather than a la carte

quote.text: people just typically nine times out of 10 they're going to choose a package
quote.speaker: Derek

tactics.name: Competitor research by attending events
steps: Attend school movie events run by others
Note what they do and how to improve
Add upgrades (themed/LED chairs, coming attractions, post-movie music)

tactics.name: Spot the next upsell by watching customers
steps: Notice kids dancing to music after the film
Source an LED dance floor
Buy triple power kit so you can run three bookings a day

quote.text: how can I monetize these kids dancing
quote.speaker: Derek

tactics.name: Ask out-of-state operators for advice
steps: Contact operators in other states (not local competitors)
Be transparent about what you're doing
Ask a couple of questions

quote.text: typically I'll reach out to people out of state cuz someone local might be like, I don't want you infringing on my business
quote.speaker: Derek

tactics.name: Negotiate with overseas manufacturers by asking what to ask
steps: Spend time with the manufacturer to get the best price
Ask them which questions you should be asking
Plan for lead times of several months

quote.text: give me the questions that I don't know to ask you
quote.speaker: Derek

warnings.warning: Consumer-grade inflatables fail in wind; his first event flopped and he had to comp it.

quote.text: It was It was a nightmare, but a great learning experience. So, I comped them

warnings.warning: Cheapest manufacturer is not always best long term; research suppliers.

warnings.warning: No repeatable lead system: reliance on Facebook Marketplace and referrals.
LED floors' music sync is poor unless the speaker is close.

lessons.lesson: Start before you're ready; the first messy job teaches what to buy.
Solve a real constraint (late sunsets) to create a category with no competitors.

quote.text: I was really trying to solve a problem because Yeah. kids are going to bed

lessons.lesson: Equipment rentals have high margins once gear is paid off; the main cost is your time.

quote.text: after I get all my um stuff purchased all it's just your time
quote.speaker: Derek

lessons.lesson: Customers who haggle aren't the target for premium offers; affluent clients on acreage pay upfront.

quote.text: if they if they say, "Oh, can I get so much off?" It's probably not for you
quote.speaker: Derek

lessons.lesson: Bundle add-ons into packages to raise average order value.
Watch how customers behave at your service to find adjacent upsells.
Obsess over the experience details (coming attractions, cold AC, hidden wiring).

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific prices and equipment costs, but revenue figures are rough estimates and the business lacks a repeatable system.
